title: Number of Nodes With Value One
summary: Given an undirected connected tree with nodes labeled from 1 to n, where the parent of node v is floor(v/2), and the root is node 1, and an array of queries to flip node values, return the count of nodes with value 1 after processing all queries.
statement: Given an undirected connected tree with nodes labeled from 1 to n, where the parent of node v is floor(v/2), and the root is node 1, and an array of queries to flip node values, return the count of nodes with value 1 after processing all queries. Each query flips the value of a node and its subtree. Flipping a node's value means changing 0 to 1 or 1 to 0.
constraints: Nodes 1 through n form an implicit binary tree where parent(v)=floor(v/2).
All values start at zero; each query flips its node and every descendant between 0 and 1.
Return the number of nodes whose final value is one.
hints: Only nodes queried an odd number of times matter; cancel even repetitions in a set.
Recursively visit the implicit tree from node one.
Carry the ancestor flip parity and toggle it when the current node is in the odd-query set.
A node’s final bit is the XOR of exactly the queried ancestors on its root path, which the recursion carries once per node.
editorial: A node’s final bit is the XOR of exactly the queried ancestors on its root path, which the recursion carries once per node.

tests.explanation: The root flip affects all nodes, the node-2 flip affects 2,4,5, and the node-5 flip affects 5; three nodes finish as one.
Flipping the entire tree twice restores every node to zero.
